sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjeet Kumar Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Sanjeet Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Ms. Ifrah Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.252 of 2023 registered under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 406 IPC at Police Station- Parikshitgarh, District Meerut with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: 4. As per prosecution story, the named accused persons, namely, Shahnawaz and Ashfaq, are stated to have taken an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- from the informant and is stated to have taken him to Saudi Arabia instead of taking to Canada and is even stated to have misled him by stating that he shall be given a job there.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has been wrongly named in the FIR as his real name isNawaz Sharif and he has been mentioned to be Shahnawaz.
Learned counsel has further stated that he has annexed the copy of the pass-port and has produced the original pass-port in Court and has stated that he has never travelled Saudi Arabia.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of theSupreme Court.
9.
In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
